_comment: Routes a lesson Pattern-Key to the PLUGIN TOOL that owns the trap it describes.
Consumed by plugin_lessons.py, which regenerates a marker-delimited segment of
one tool's `description` string inside the MCP server's own source.
WHY A SEPARATE FILE FROM skill_lesson_routes.json
A skill block and a tool description are different surfaces with different
economics, so they must be budgeted separately:
skill block        loads only when that skill loads.  Costs nothing otherwise.
tool description   is in context for EVERY session where the plugin is
connected, whether or not the trap is relevant.
So the bar here is HIGHER, not lower. A rule earns a place in a description
only if the mistake it prevents is made while CALLING THAT TOOL. Anything
broader belongs in the companion skill.
WHICH SERVERS ARE ELIGIBLE
Only servers Jordan owns. Measured 2026-09-03 from the launch commands:
8933  node CommandBridge\batch-exec-server.js        eligible - own code
8934  node FlowBridge\flow-mcp-server.js             eligible - own code
8932  npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem  NOT eligible - upstream
8931  npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest                   NOT eligible - upstream
An edit to an npx-launched package lands in node_modules and is overwritten on
the next start. For 8931/8932 the durable surface is the companion skill,
which skill_lesson_routes.json already covers.
MARKERS ARE PLACED BY HAND, ONCE
Unlike the skill applier, this one NEVER inserts markers into a file that has
none. Choosing an insertion point in arbitrary JavaScript is not a safe
automatic operation - a markdown file has an unambiguous first H2, a source
file does not. Place the pair by hand inside the description expression, get
it reviewed, and the applier owns regeneration from then on.
prefix - any Pattern-Key starting with this string
exact  - a full Pattern-Key
Nothing here DELETES a lesson. cowork-lessons.md stays the authoritative home
for every entry; a routed entry gains a Delivered-to pointer naming the tool.
Decided 2026-09-03: delivery is not promotion, so an integrated lesson is
never retired from the corpus.

command-bridge-8933.title: the approved batch executor (8933)
_note: BYTES RECLAIMED 2026-09-03: bridge-8933-arg-name was REMOVED from this
route after verify_delivery.py returned INERT - 3 of 3 carried runs passed
AND so did the control. All four independently reported taking the
parameter name from the tool's INPUT SCHEMA, not from this prose.
That is the general principle, and it is worth applying before adding any
future rule here: a rule that restates a machine-readable schema
constraint is inert by construction. `properties.file` plus
`required: [file]` plus `additionalProperties: false` already makes every
wrong parameter name impossible, and the schema is enforced where prose is
merely read. Prose earns its always-on bytes only where the schema cannot
reach - runtime behaviour, ordering, and traps that look like success.
The entry stays in cowork-lessons.md; only the delivery was withdrawn.
EXACT ONLY, DELIBERATELY. The first draft of this route used the prefixes
`bridge-8933-` and `batch-`, copying skill_lesson_routes.json. Running it
on the real corpus showed why that is wrong here: prefix matching pulled in
bridge-8933-stateless-defeats-in-process-state (a rule about WRITING a
bridge server) and batch-gui-launcher-defeats-timeout-guard (a niche rule
about probing unknown binaries), filling 95% of the budget with prose that
does not fire while calling this tool.
Prefix matching is fine for a skill block, which costs nothing until the
skill loads. It is wrong for a description, which every session pays for.
The test for inclusion here is narrow: does this mistake get made while
CALLING run_batch_file? If it is made while BUILDING the bridge, it belongs
in the command-bridge skill, which already carries it.
bridge-8932-writes-lf is routed here even though it names the OTHER bridge:
the LF damage is done by the filesystem bridge but it BITES when cmd parses
the .bat, which happens here. The trap belongs to the tool where it fires.
The static description currently carries three of these rules TYPED BY HAND
(arg name, CRLF, transport drop). Hand copies drift - see the lesson
enforcer-encodes-the-superseded-rule. Replacing them with a generated
segment is the whole point of this route.
NOT routed here: bridge-absent-probe-is-not-permanent and the other
bridge-ABSENT rules. The server's own reminderBlock() already says why -
a description cannot reach a session that never calls the tool, and an
absent bridge is exactly that case. Those stay in copilot-instructions.md.

power-automate-8934.title: the Power Automate bridge (8934)
_note: The prefix follows the house convention bridge-<port>-, matching the
existing bridge-8932- and bridge-8933- keys. An earlier draft used
flowbridge-evaluate-, which matched nothing and would have rendered an
empty segment forever while looking correctly configured.
Scoped to the evaluate_ prefix rather than all of bridge-8934- on purpose:
this route writes into ONE tool's description, so it must not collect
rules about the other 28 tools. A lesson about resubmit_run or the
solution ALM tools needs its own route entry naming its own tool.
First occupant: bridge-8934-evaluate-rejects-safe-navigation, logged
2026-09-03 - the ?[] optional accessor is refused with 'unexpected
character ?' while the same expression without the ? evaluates.
